title: Assistant Management Accountant
description:
Assistant Management Accountant Fast-Growing SME Retail Business
- Permanent
- SW London - Kingston upon Thames
- Salary depending on experience 38,000 - 45,000
- 4 Days in HQ - Stunning offices!
- Flexi hours + Bonus + study support + discounts and much more

The Opportunity

An exciting opportunity has arisen for an experienced Assistant Management Accountant to join a fast-paced and growing SME retail business.

This is a genuinely hands-on role within a lean Finance team, offering excellent exposure across the full month-end process and the wider business. It would suit someone who enjoys getting into the detail, takes ownership of their work and wants to be part of a team where everyone plays an important role.

You'll work closely with the Commercial Finance Manager and operational stakeholders, helping to ensure the numbers are accurate, processes are robust and month-end runs smoothly.

What You'll Be Doing
- Taking ownership of key areas of the month-end process from start to finish
- Preparing and posting journals, accruals and prepayments
- Completing balance sheet reconciliations and investigating outstanding items
- Taking responsibility for regular bank reconciliations, ensuring discrepancies are identified and resolved
- Supporting the preparation of monthly management accounts
- Investigating variances and financial queries, getting to the root cause and following through to resolution
- Supporting cashbook and control account activities
- Ensuring financial information is accurate, complete and delivered within agreed deadlines
- Working closely with colleagues across Finance and the wider business to resolve queries
- Helping to improve processes, controls and ways of working as the business continues to grow
- Providing support across the wider Finance function and getting involved wherever needed

What We're Looking For

We're looking for someone who is hands-on, commercially aware and naturally detail-focused Assistant Management Accountant, with the confidence to take ownership rather than waiting to be told what to do.

Ideally, you will have:
- Experience in an Assistant Management Accountant, Assistant Accountant or similar role
- Strong month-end experience, including journals, accruals, prepayments and reconciliations
- Excellent bank reconciliation experience and the ability to investigate and resolve discrepancies
- Ideally, experience within an SME or lean Finance environment where you have genuinely been involved in the detail
- A strong understanding of financial controls and the importance of accurate financial information
- The ability to manage multiple priorities and work to tight deadlines
- A proactive and solutions-focused approach
- Excellent attention to detail and a real pride in getting things right
- A collaborative approach and willingness to support the wider team
- The confidence to question, investigate and improve rather than simply process

AAT, ACCA or CIMA studies would be beneficial, but practical experience, attitude and the ability to take ownership are just as important.

Why This Role?

This is a great opportunity for someone who wants more than a narrow transactional role.

You'll be joining a fast-paced, growing retail business where you can really get under the bonnet of the numbers, work closely with the wider business and make a visible contribution.

If you enjoy variety, like being hands-on and want to develop within a supportive Finance team where your contribution

title: Legal Administrator
description:
We are seeking a highly organised and detail-focused Legal Support Assistant for one of our local authority clients.

Rate advertsied on CV Library is Umbrella PAYE.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced administrator who enjoys working in a professional environment, managing a varied workload and supporting the delivery of high-quality legal services.

You will play a vital role in ensuring the smooth operation of the department through effective document management, financial administration, case management support and general business administration.

Working closely with legal professionals and colleagues across the organisation, you will help maintain accurate records, support governance processes and contribute to the effective delivery of services for Westminster's residents and stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities
- Document Management
- Prepare, collate and paginate documentation for hearings, contracts, agreements and meetings.
- Redact documents accurately and in accordance with relevant procedures.
- Maintain accurate filing systems and support the retrieval of legal documents and deeds.
- Signing and Sealing

- Maintain statutory and corporate registers accurately.
- Financial Administration

- Liaise with suppliers and internal stakeholders to resolve payment queries.

- Produce reports and management information from departmental systems.
- Manage incoming and outgoing post and shared mailboxes.
- Order stationery and undertake photocopying, scanning and document preparation.
- Organise meetings, take minutes and maintain accurate records.
- Respond professionally and promptly to internal and external enquiries.
- Provide planned and ad-hoc support for colleagues to ensure service continuity.

title: Medical Secretary - Private GP Healthcare
description:
Medical Secretary - Private GP Practice - Central London - 13 month maternity cover - 42k to 45k

A well-established private GP practice based in the Chelsea area of London, is looking for an experienced Medical Secretary to join the professional, friendly, and established team on a 13-month fixed-term maternity cover contract. This post will be supporting 2 senior GPs, as well as playing an important role in the smooth day-to-day running of the practice and coordination of patient care.

You will be highly organised, proactive and confident working independently in a busy private healthcare environment. Excellent communication skills, attention to detail and a strong understanding of patient confidentiality are essential, as well as being able to present a professional and empathetic service to the patients.

SALARY ETC:
- 42k to 45k + Benefits
- Central London, Chelsea area.
- Starting on 1st December, neg, for a 13 month maternity cover contract.
- Full-time, Monday-Friday, approximately 8:30am-6:00pm, office based.

REQUIREMENTS:
- 5 years' + private sector medical secretarial experience, ideally within private healthcare in London.
- Experience within private general practice would be particularly advantageous
- A good working knowledge of medical terminology, as well as strong administrative and organisational skills
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills
- Confidence dealing directly with private patients, consultants, hospitals and insurance companies
- Experience using a private healthcare patient-management system such as Semble experience would be highly desirable
- A stable employment history, ideally demonstrating at least two continuous years within previous roles
- AMSPAR or Pitman qualifications are desirable but not essential
- Must be smart in appearance, with a professional and customer/patient orientated approach.

DUTIES TO INCLUDE:
- Extensive diary and appointment management, Managing patient enquiries by telephone and email
- Managing doctors' inboxes and ensuring patient queries are dealt with promptly
- Processing repeat prescriptions, arranging hospital admissions, investigations and diagnostic tests
- Chasing outstanding pathology results, diagnostic reports and consultant letters, Processing patient recalls and follow-up requirements
- Reviewing incoming clinical correspondence and updating patient records on Semble
- Preparing and coordinating referrals, medical reports, insurance forms and certificates
- Processing referral letters, clinical notes and outgoing patient correspondence
- Invoicing patients following consultations and ensuring payment is collected, Processing card payments and insurance-company payments, Chasing outstanding patient debt
- Correcting and updating invoices where required
- Completing end-of-day transaction checks
- Supporting vaccine and medication stock ordering
- Providing cover for other members of the secretarial team during periods of leave or sickness
- Supporting the doctors and wider practice team with additional administrative duties as required

Due to the high volume of applications we receive, we regret that we are unable to respond individually to every applicant. If you have not heard from us within 2 weeks of the closing date, please assume that your application has not been successful on this occasion. We sincerely thank you for your interest and wish you every success in your job search

title: Financial Accounts Assistant
description:
Financial Accounts Assistant

Salary: 38,000 - 48,000 depending on experience.

Location: Piccadilly Circus (FULL TIME IN OFFICE

Discretionary bonus.

Competitive pension contribution.

Private medical insurance.

Life assurance.

Additional salary sacrifices benefits and wellbeing support.

The Company

Our client is a privately owned group with a diverse portfolio of businesses operating across multiple sectors, including financial services, technology, real estate, energy, healthcare, media and other commercial industries.

The Position

Reports to: Chief Accountant

Primary Focus: Cash book management, maintenance of accounting records and support with year-end accounts.

Role Purpose

To maintain complete, accurate and timely accounting records across several UK and international entities. The role will have particular responsibility for cash book management, day-to-day treasury activities and maintaining financial records. The successful candidate will support cash management, banking controls, reporting requirements, statutory compliance and the year-end audit process.

Key Responsibilities

Cash Book & Accounting Records
- Maintain cash book records, ensuring receipts, payments, transfers, bank charges, interest and other transactions are accurately recorded.
- Post cash book transactions to the relevant nominal ledger accounts, cost centres and intercompany accounts with supporting documentation.
- Prepare and process payments through online banking platforms in line with company procedures and approval processes.
- Perform regular bank reconciliations and investigate outstanding items promptly.
- Maintain sales and purchase ledgers, including processing invoices, allocating receipts and payments, and resolving queries.
- Support month-end processes, including accruals, prepayments and journal postings.
- Ensure strong financial controls are maintained, including appropriate approval procedures for payments and transfers.

Management Reporting
- Prepare cash flow and treasury information for management reporting.
- Investigate and explain significant cash flow movements and variances.
- Assist with the preparation of management accounts and reporting packs.
- Support stakeholders with financial information and analysis.

Audit, Tax & Compliance
- Prepare schedules and supporting documentation for year-end audits.
- Respond to auditor queries and assist with bank confirmation requests.
- Support VAT returns and other statutory reporting requirements.
- Ensure accounting records remain accurate and audit-ready.

Wider Finance Responsibilities
- Assist with ledger reconciliations and general finance activities.
- Support budgeting, forecasting and performance reporting.
- Contribute to group reporting and consolidation activities where required.
- Undertake ad hoc financial analysis and projects.

Essential Skills & Experience
- Strong experience of bank reconciliations, cash book management and ledger activities.
- Experience supporting treasury operations, payment processes and cash flow forecasting.
- Advanced Excel skills and good working knowledge of accounting systems.
- Comfortable using AI and automation tools to improve reporting and finance processes.
- Strong analytical skills with excellent attention to detail.
- Understanding of financial controls, approvals and compliance procedures.
- Strong communication skills with the ability to explain financial information to non-finance stakeholders.

Personal Qualities
- Highly trustworthy with the ability to handle confidential information.
- Organised, proactive and able to work independently.
- Strong time management skills with the ability to meet deadlines.
- Solution-focused with a continuous improvement mindset.
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.

title: Part-Time Payroll Assistant
description:
A City-led international firm with 1,000 employees, and offices across the UK, the Middle East and Asia, are looking to recruit an experienced Part-Time Payroll Assistant to work 4 days a week.

The Role

As a Part-Time Payroll Assistant, you will play an important role in ensuring the accurate and timely delivery of the firm's monthly payroll.

Working as part of a small, collaborative team, you will be responsible for a range of payroll administration duties, including processing starters and leavers, payroll changes, overtime, benefits, pension updates, statutory payments and month-end reporting using the ADP/NGUX payroll system.

You will also act as a point of contact for employee payroll queries, resolving issues professionally, efficiently and with discretion.

Key Responsibilities
- Process employee starters and leavers accurately using the ADP/NGUX payroll system.
- Respond to and resolve employee payroll queries, including tax-related issues and system login problems.
- Process monthly payroll changes and produce ad hoc reports as required.
- Manage monthly overtime forms and reconcile the information against payroll system outputs.
- Calculate and process monthly sickness payments in accordance with the firm's policies.
- Prepare statutory parental leave payment schedules and verify calculations using the HMRC calculator.
- Administer monthly employee benefits and pension variations within the payroll system.
- Raise and process casual and ad hoc employee payments.
- Check and process monthly HMRC/PAYE payments following payroll sign-off.
- Prepare and deliver month-end reporting to the Benefits team.
- Undertake additional payroll and administrative duties as required, reflecting the varied responsibilities of a small team.

Skills, Experience and Requirements
- Proven experience using the ADP/NGUX payroll platform is essential.
- Previous experience in a payroll administration role, ideally within the professional services sector.
- Understanding of manual tax and National Insurance (NI) calculations.
- Good Microsoft Excel skills.
- Up-to-date knowledge of HMRC statutory regulations and payroll requirements.
- Excellent attention to detail and a high level of numerical accuracy.
- Strong organisational and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and meet tight deadlines.
- High levels of discretion and integrity when handling confidential and sensitive employee information.
- A proactive, flexible and collaborative approach to working within a small team.

Qualifications
- A CIPP (Chartered Institute of Payroll Professionals) qualification is desirable but not essential.

title: Document Controller
description:
An excellent opportunity has arisen for two experienced Document Controllers to join an established construction and building services business in London.

The successful candidates will be responsible for managing and maintaining project documentation throughout the lifecycle of construction projects, ensuring that drawings, technical information, submissions, correspondence and other project records are accurately controlled, distributed and kept up to date.

This is an ideal opportunity for a Document Controller who has previous experience working within the construction, M&E, mechanical, electrical or building services sector and is looking to join an established project team on a permanent basis.

Key Responsibilities
- Manage the day-to-day document control process across construction projects.
- Receive, register, distribute and track project documentation.
- Maintain accurate electronic and hard-copy filing systems.
- Control the issue and revision of drawings and technical documentation.
- Ensure project teams are working from the latest approved information.
- Upload and distribute drawings, specifications, technical submissions and other project information.
- Monitor document revisions and maintain accurate revision histories.
- Liaise with Project Managers, Site Managers, Engineers, Quantity Surveyors, consultants, subcontractors and clients.
- Chase outstanding documentation and ensure information is received within agreed timescales.
- Carry out document quality checks before information is issued.
- Maintain document registers and produce regular reports when required.
- Assist project teams with the preparation and collation of O&M manuals and handover documentation.
- Ensure documentation is managed in accordance with company and client procedures.
- Maintain confidentiality and security of project information.
- Support the project team with general administration relating to document control and information management.

Requirements

The successful candidate will ideally have:
- Previous experience working as a Document Controller within the construction industry.
- Experience working for a main contractor, M&E contractor, specialist subcontractor or building services company.
- Good understanding of construction drawings, specifications, technical submissions and project documentation.
- Experience using electronic document management systems.
- Experience with platforms such as Aconex, Viewpoint, 4 Projects, Asite, Procore, SharePoint or similar would be advantageous.
- Excellent organisational and administration skills.
- Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
- The ability to manage multiple projects, deadlines and priorities.
- Good communication skills and the confidence to liaise with project teams, clients and subcontractors.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, Word and Outlook.
- A proactive approach and the ability to work independently as well as part of a wider project team.

Desirable Experience

Experience within M&E / MEP, mechanical, electrical, HVAC or building services would be particularly advantageous.

Candidates with experience managing documentation on large commercial, residential, infrastructure or major building services projects are encouraged to apply.

title: Credit Controller
description:
Credit Controller

£34,000 - £36,000 Central London Hybrid - 3 days office / 2 days home Permanent Immediate Start

An exciting opportunity has arisen for an experienced Credit Controller to join the finance team of a rapidly expanding international business based in Central London.

This is a varied credit control position within a commercially focused organisation where you'll have responsibility for a diverse customer ledger and work closely with colleagues across Finance, Sales and Operations.

The role would suit an experienced Credit Controller who enjoys having ownership of their accounts, building strong customer relationships and taking a proactive approach to recovering outstanding payments. NetSuite experience is highly desirable, as you'll be using the system regularly to monitor accounts, review balances and maintain accurate financial information.

About the Role:

As Credit Controller, you'll be responsible for keeping customer accounts up to date and ensuring outstanding invoices are followed up effectively.

You'll take a structured approach to your ledger, identifying overdue accounts, investigating issues and agreeing payment solutions with customers. You'll also work closely with internal departments where billing, contractual or account queries are preventing payment.

Experience dealing with complicated invoices, underpayments and legacy payments will be very beneficial. Further experience conducting investigations into aged debt and outstanding invoices will be very a great asset for this credit control role.

There may also be opportunities to support finance and operational teams during major events, giving the role a broader commercial dimension than a traditional credit control position.

Key Duties:
- Take day-to-day responsibility for an allocated customer ledger.
- Monitor outstanding invoices and carry out regular collection activity.
- Contact customers by telephone and email to agree payment dates and resolve overdue balances.
- Review aged debt and determine appropriate follow-up actions.
- Maintain accurate notes and records of collection activity.
- Investigate account discrepancies, invoice queries and disputed balances.
- Produce customer statements and respond to account-related enquiries.
- Work with Sales and other departments to resolve issues affecting payment.
- Reconcile customer and sales information between internal systems and NetSuite.
- Help minimise aged debt, credit notes and unallocated cash.
- Ensure payments are chased ahead of key event and operational deadlines.
- Maintain accurate customer account information.
- Deal confidently with customers across different markets and currencies.
- Provide assistance to on-site teams with customer payments when required.

We're particularly interested in candidates who have:
- Solid Credit Control or Accounts Receivable experience.
- Previous experience using NetSuite.
- Good Excel skills.
- Experience dealing with multi-currency accounts and international customers.
- A good understanding of VAT and financial processes.
- Excellent communication and negotiation skills.
- The confidence to deal with customers regarding overdue payments.
- Strong attention to detail and numerical accuracy.
- Good organisation and the ability to prioritise a busy workload.
- A proactive approach to resolving problems rather than simply reporting them.
- Experience within events, exhibitions, media or another fast-moving commercial environment would be advantageous.

The Working Environment

The company has an informal and sociable culture, offering a refreshing alternative to a traditional corporate finance environment.

You'll be working in a relaxed office with a casual dress code, alongside a team that regularly gets together for social events, celebrations and nights out.

The business is continuing to grow internationally, so this is an opportunity to join a finance function where there is plenty of activity and exposure to different areas of the organisation.

Package:
- Salary: £34,000 - £36,000
- Location: Central London
- Hybrid: 3 days in the office / 2 days from home
- Start: Immediate
- Holiday: 25 days + 8 bank holidays
- Pension: Company pension scheme
- Additional benefits: Cycle to Work scheme and Season Ticket Loan

title: Credit Controller
description:
My client is looking for an experienced and proactive Credit Controller to join our Finance Department. The successful candidate will take responsibility for managing customer accounts, controlling credit exposure, collecting outstanding debts and ensuring customer accounts and payment allocations are accurate and up to date. The role requires close coordination with the Billing Department and regular reporting to the Finance Manager and Finance Director on collections and expected cash receipts for cash-flow planning.

Main Duties
- Proactively manage the sales ledger and collect outstanding customer debts by telephone and email.
- Monitor live customer balances, credit limits and credit utilisation daily.
- Contact customers approaching their credit limits and provide statements where required.
- Place customers exceeding their approved credit limit or payment terms on stop, and remove accounts from stop promptly once payment has been received and allocated.
- Communicate account stop/release information to the relevant operational departments.
- Contact customers before invoices become due to confirm invoices have been received, are correct and are approved for payment.
- Work closely with the Billing Department to resolve missing invoices, invoice queries and disputes promptly so that payments are not unnecessarily delayed.
- Maintain accurate expected payment dates and collection notes and provide the Finance Manager and Finance Director with regular updates on collections and expected cash receipts.
- Maintain and regularly review the aged debtor report, identifying overdue, disputed and high-risk accounts.
- Allocate customer receipts accurately to Sage, including BACS, cheque and credit-card payments.
- Reconcile daily credit-card transactions and receipts against payment-provider reports, the invoicing system and bank receipts.
- Maintain credit-card reconciliation records and investigate any differences promptly.
- Process and reconcile non-account/customer card transactions and related invoices, ensuring payments and invoices are correctly matched and recorded.
- Produce and issue customer statements and overdue-payment correspondence.
- Process credit-note requests, ensuring the correct supporting information and approval is obtained before credit notes are raised and issued.
- Record disputed invoices accurately and coordinate with Billing to ensure disputes are investigated and resolved.
- Evaluate new credit applications and carry out credit checks using Credit Reference Agencies.
- Maintain approved customer credit limits and payment terms.
- Complete regular reconciliations between Sage 50 Accounts Professional, Waste Logic and other relevant payment/invoicing systems.
- Deal promptly with customer account queries and manage the Credit Control mailbox.
- Ensure customer accounts, payment allocations, credit-control notes and supporting records remain accurate and fully up to date.

Experience & Skills

The successful candidate should have strong previous Credit Control experience and be confident managing a busy debtor ledger, chasing payments and dealing directly with customers. Experience of payment allocation, credit-card reconciliation, aged debt management, credit limits, account stops, customer reconciliations and invoice disputes is important.

The candidate must be proactive, organised and confident communicating with customers and internal departments. Strong attention to detail and reconciliation skills are essential. Experience using Sage 50 Accounts Professional is highly desirable, and experience with Waste Logic or similar waste-management/invoicing software would be an advantage. Previous experience within the construction, recycling, waste management or haulage industry would also be advantageous.

title: Personal Assistant
description:
My client, a vibrant, growing community that serves over 3.2 million people including 470 parishes, 144 schools, and 579 churches based across East London and Essex are recruiting for a Personal assistant to the Archdeacon.

The Archdeacon resources, advises and directs clergy and lay officers in the Anglican parishes of the Archdeaconry of West Ham and often represents their joint interests at diocesan meetings and at the local parochial level.

The suitable candidate will act as the primary point of contact for the Archdeacon s office and is responsible for providing diary management and the organisation of meetings, as well as providing full administration support to the duties undertaken by the Archdeacon s office. You will work close to the Archdeacon s home.

Duties in more detail (but not subject to):
- To manage the Archdeacon s calendar and appointments in an accurate and efficient manner.
- To provide high-quality support to the Archdeacon in preparation for key meetings and forums, including the collation of relevant documentation, creating agendas, preparing and distributing minutes, highlighting actions
- To attend and take minutes or notes at meetings when required.
- To respond proactively to enquiries and queries addressed to the Archdeacon s office, including drafting correspondence, following these up with the appropriate action or redirecting for actions.
- To manage visitors to the Archdeacon s office, providing hospitality and a warm welcome
- To carry out research on the web, or elsewhere, on topics relating to the Archdeacon s ministry and where necessary provide this in a user-friendly format.
- To manage the arrangements for vacancy meetings, including liaising with parishes, senior colleagues and patrons
- To administer the appointment processes (recruitment) for clergy and other roles (liaises with parishes, candidates, referees, Diocesan Registry), including placing vacancy adverts with the relevant media sites, recording applications, and conducting background checks and references.
- To administer the DBS Applications renewal process for current Diocesan clergy, ensuring applications are initiated prior to current certificates expiring
- To arrange training events and under the guidance of the Archdeacon prepare relevant documentation as well as ensuring the provision of training materials, including the annual training for new churchwardens.
- Maintain supply of stationery and sundry items (tea, coffee etc.).

Essential s to be considered for the role:
- At least A Level standard or equivalent level of education.
- Having an understanding of the Church of England/Diocese of Chelmsford and the Christian faith.
- Proven professional PA/ administration support at a senior level.
- Experience of managing diaries and arranging meetings with multiple stakeholders on Teams/Zoom and face to face.
- Experience of Office 365 (or equivalent) Excel, Zoom, Teams and Electronic Diary Systems.
- Experience of drafting emails and correspondence relating to routine and non-routine matters.
- A self-starter and able to confidently work on own initiative, ensuring tasks are prioritised.
- Able and motivated to work alone at times, including under pressure.
- Able to occasionally travel across the Diocese.
- Holds a current valid Driving Licence and access to private transport with insurance for travel on business purposes

The vacancy is an ideal opportunity for a self-starter with experience of working as a PA.

The post holder will apply discretion and diplomacy in their work and be competent to manage much of the work on their own

Closing date is 11th October with in-person interviews taking place on 22 October.

All appointments are subject to acceptable pre-employment checks, including a satisfactory Basic DBS check.

title: Activity Co-ordinator
description:
JOB DESCRIPTION

Position Title: Activity Coordinator

Reports To: Service Manager or Team Leader

SOUTH WEST LONDON

Roles Reporting to this Position: None

Primary Objective: To design, coordinate and deliver a varied programme of engaging, accessible and employment-focused activities for young people aged 18 to 24. The role will build aspiration, confidence, resilience, transferable skills and understanding of workplace expectations, while working closely with Mentors and partners to help each participant progress towards suitable and sustainable employment, education or training.

Key Relationships/Interactions

Internal

Service Manager and Team Leader

Mentors and Employer Engagement and Employer Services colleagues

Quality, Compliance, Performance, Safeguarding and MI teams

Wider Delivery Colleagues

External

Participants (young people aged 18 to 24) and, where appropriate and with consent, their support networks

Engagement Activity Partners, specialist subcontractors and community organisations

Jobcentre Plus, local authorities, education and training providers

Local employers, sector partners and venue providers

Key Responsibilities

Activity Design and Delivery

Design, coordinate and maintain a rolling programme of structured group and individual activities aligned with participants needs, aspirations, action plans and outcomes.

Deliver welcoming, energetic and inclusive sessions for young people aged 18 to 24, using age-appropriate interests such as sport, creative arts, technology, gaming, virtual reality, outdoor activities and community projects.

Prepare clear session plans, learning objectives, resources and contingency arrangements so every activity supports employability, personal development or progression.

Adapt pace, content and delivery for different communication styles, neurodiversity, disabilities, literacy levels, digital capability, confidence levels and reasonable-adjustment needs.

Participant Engagement and Development

Use trauma-informed, strengths-based and culturally responsive practice to build trust, promote participant choice and voice, and support those who lack confidence or have had negative experiences of services or education.

Help participants develop communication, teamwork, problem-solving, resilience, timekeeping, professional behaviours, digital skills and an understanding of workplace expectations.

Support young people to identify and present their transferable skills and achievements in CVs, applications, interviews and employer conversations.

Provide practical sector insight through employer talks, workplace visits, careers activities, mock recruitment exercises, volunteering and project-based learning.

Coordination and Partnership Working

Coordinate specialist partner delivery, including procurement or booking processes, schedules, venues, participant communications, accessibility, risk information, attendance, feedback and supporting evidence.

Work closely with Mentors to identify suitable activities, share relevant progress or concerns, and ensure learning is reflected in participant action plans and next steps.

Promote activities through engaging face-to-face and digital communications, use reminders and motivational contact, and promptly follow up non-attendance with the Mentor.

Build relationships with youth, community, education, health, specialist and employer partners to widen participation, strengthen referral routes and reduce barriers.

Contribute to programme events, outreach, sector pathways and employment-focused campaigns across sites and community venues.

Safeguarding, Inclusion and Professional Practice

Place participant welfare at the centre of delivery and follow safeguarding, lone-working, incident, whistleblowing and escalation procedures at all times.

Recognise and respond appropriately to safeguarding concerns, disclosures, exploitation risks or changes in presentation. Apply adult safeguarding procedures for participants aged 18 to 24 and follow child safeguarding processes where a concern also involves a child.

Maintain professional boundaries, confidentiality and appropriate use of digital communication and social media.

Obtain and record informed consent where required, share information only where there is an appropriate and lawful basis and comply with data protection requirements.

Quality, Compliance and Performance

Complete activity and venue risk assessments, dynamic risk checks, incident reports and emergency arrangements in line with organisational policy and health and safety requirements.

Maintain accurate, timely and audit-ready records of referrals, attendance, participation, adjustments, feedback, progress, outcomes, risk documentation and safeguarding actions.

Deliver the agreed activity schedule consistently, ensuring sessions start on time and resources, venues and partners are coordinated effectively.

Monitor attendance, engagement and completion, take timely action to address non-engagement, and evidence improvements in confidence, employability skills, workplace understanding and readiness for next steps.

Use participant and stakeholder feedback, attendance data and progression information to evaluate impact and continuously improve the activity offer.

Support progression to agreed next steps, including mentoring actions, training, employer engagement, interviews, work experience or employment.

Manage activity resources and agreed budgets responsibly, demonstrate value for money, and ensure equipment is safe, available and stored appropriately.

Professional Knowledge and Flexibility

Maintain current knowledge of youth employment challenges, local labour markets, digital trends and support available to 18 to 24-year-olds.

Work flexibly across locations and, where required, outside standard hours to meet participant and programme needs.

To deliver role responsibilities in line with organisational values and all relevant policies and procedures

Any other duties appropriate to the level of this role, for which the post-holder has the necessary training or experience.

Essential and Desirable Skills, Knowledge and Experience

Delivery and Engagement

Experience of planning, coordinating and delivering engaging group activities for young people or young adults, preferably including those aged 18 to 24 and those not in education, employment or training or facing multiple barriers.

Strong facilitation, presentation and engagement skills, with the ability to build rapport while maintaining clear boundaries and expectations.

Ability to turn creative or recreational activities into purposeful employability and personal-development learning and adapt delivery for different needs, abilities, cultures, communication styles and confidence levels.

Experience in employability, youth work, community development, education, careers, coaching or publicly funded services, including delivery of creative, digital, sports, gaming, virtual reality, outdoor, volunteering or project-based activities.

Participant Support and Safe Practice

Understanding of barriers affecting young people, including low confidence, poor mental wellbeing, disability, neurodiversity, caring responsibilities, housing instability, transport difficulties, digital exclusion and limited work experience.

Knowledge of adult and child safeguarding responsibilities, professional boundaries, equality,

Qualifications, Values and Flexibility

A relevant qualification in youth work, teaching, training, coaching, careers, employability, safeguarding, mental health first aid or facilitation.

A current first-aid qualification and experience of completing activity or venue risk assessments.

Commitment to participant voice, strengths-based practice, inclusion and high-quality customer service.

Ability and willingness to travel on a daily basis to different locations within assigned local area, to support participants, employers, events, placements and contract delivery (no homeworking is available due to the nature of the role)

Willingness to complete all required induction and refresher training, including safeguarding, equality, data protection and health and safety.

Appointment is subject to checks appropriate to the role and participant group, which may include a DBS check where legally eligible and required.

title: Youth Opportunities Coordinator
description:
Single Homeless Project has a new opportunity for a Youth Opportunities Coordinator ?to join our team based in Greenwich, London. You will join us on a full-time, permanent basis and, in return, receive a competitive salary starting at £29,822.41 and rising incrementally to £32,034.46 per annum.

We re London s leading homelessness charity and we get things done.

In a city where hundreds are forced into homelessness every day, our work has never been more needed or more challenging. And we re not shying away. We re rolling up our sleeves to make change and helping over 10,000 Londoners every year. We prevent homelessness, provide safe places to live and give people the opportunity to rebuild their lives and transform their futures. And we never give up.

We re here for Londoners wherever they are on their journey. We start with trust, building relationships that help people feel safe, supported, and ready to move forward. Every day, we put people first in everything we do, challenging injustice and barriers that keep people from the safety, stability and opportunity they deserve. We stand alongside people as they rebuild and shape a future that feels their own.

Joining Single Homeless Project means joining a team that s bold, compassionate and determined to do better for the people we support and for each other. You ll work alongside colleagues with lived experience, in a space that s trans-inclusive, disability-friendly, and actively striving to be anti-oppressive and equitable.

We re not perfect, but we re real. We listen. We learn. And we push forward, together. Because this isn t just a job. It s a chance to lead with empathy, spark change, and help build a London where no one is left behind.

About the Youth Opportunities Coordinator role:

For a young person who has felt stuck, disconnected or unsure what comes next, the right opportunity can be the thing that changes everything. As our Youth Opportunities Coordinator in Greenwich, you ll create the spaces, experiences and encouragement that help young people build confidence, discover what they are capable of and take meaningful steps towards greater independence.

You ll lead a varied programme of activities across our young person's accommodation services, bringing together opportunities around education, training and employment, life skills, wellbeing, creativity, sport, pre-tenancy preparation and personal development. Some sessions you ll deliver yourself; others you ll shape alongside colleagues, community organisations and specialist providers. The aim is simple: make the programme relevant, engaging and worth showing up for.

A big part of the role is understanding what can sit behind disengagement. You ll work creatively with young people who may be NEET (young people who are not currently in education, employment or training), have experienced trauma or struggled to engage with traditional services, using psychologically informed, trauma-informed and person-centred approaches to build trust and motivation. You ll also coach frontline colleagues to run effective activities of their own, helping opportunities become part of everyday life across the services.

This is a role with real scope to create, test and improve. You ll be part of a wider Opportunities team, sharing ideas and good practice while developing your own expertise in youth engagement, group work and programme delivery. You ll also have access to Single Homeless Project's (SHP) learning and development opportunities, helping you build specialist skills to grow your career across the organisation.

About you as our Youth Opportunities Coordinator:
- You know how to connect with young people who may be reluctant to engage, and can turn curiosity, creativity and persistence into meaningful participation.
- You have experience designing, coordinating or delivering engaging groups, activities or programmes for young people.

description:
Single Homeless Project has a new opportunity for a Housing Pathway Coordinator ?to join our team based in Camden, London. You will join us on a full-time, permanent basis and, in return, receive a competitive salary starting at £34,127.11 and rising incrementally to £36,947.49 per annum.

We re London s leading homelessness charity and we get things done.

In a city where hundreds are forced into homelessness every day, our work has never been more needed or more challenging. And we re not shying away. We re rolling up our sleeves to make change and helping over 10,000 Londoners every year. We prevent homelessness, provide safe places to live and give people the opportunity to rebuild their lives and transform their futures. And we never give up.

We re here for Londoners wherever they are on their journey. We start with trust, building relationships that help people feel safe, supported, and ready to move forward. Every day, we put people first in everything we do, challenging injustice and barriers that keep people from the safety, stability and opportunity they deserve. We stand alongside people as they rebuild and shape a future that feels their own.

Joining Single Homeless Project means joining a team that s bold, compassionate and determined to do better for the people we support and for each other. You ll work alongside colleagues with lived experience, in a space that s trans-inclusive, disability-friendly, and actively striving to be anti-oppressive and equitable.

We re not perfect, but we re real. We listen. We learn. And we push forward, together. Because this isn t just a job. It s a chance to lead with empathy, spark change, and help build a London where no one is left behind.

About the Housing Pathway Coordinator role:

Rough sleeping pathways only work when the system around people moves with urgency, consistency and accountability. This role is about making sure people sleeping rough, or at risk of returning to the streets, are not left waiting, drifting between services, or losing accommodation because barriers have not been gripped quickly enough.

As Outreach Housing Pathway Coordinator, you will work within Camden s integrated Rough Sleeping and Outreach Hub to help people access and sustain appropriate accommodation. You will hold oversight of where people are in their housing journey, identify what is blocking progress, and work with outreach teams, Navigators, hostels, pathway providers, community safety partners and statutory services to keep plans moving.

You will focus on the points where pathways can break down: delays, exclusions, unsuitable offers, unresolved risks, street activity linked to accommodation, or support needs that have not yet been fully understood or responded to. Through assertive engagement, practical case coordination and strong partnership working, you will help people stabilise their accommodation and reduce the risk of returning to rough sleeping.

Working within Camden s No Wrong Door model, you will bring grip, judgement and persistence to complex situations, ensuring people experiencing multiple disadvantage receive a response that is joined-up, trauma-informed and focused on lasting routes away from the street. SHP will support you with the training, reflective practice and development opportunities needed to continue building your expertise in this work.

About you as our Housing Pathway Coordinator:
- You understand that people experiencing rough sleeping are often navigating trauma, exclusion, unmet needs and systems that have not worked for them. You bring patience, persistence and a clear belief that people should not be written off when engagement is difficult.
- You know how homelessness pathways, outreach services and supported accommodation can work together, and you can spot where delays, exclusions or gaps in communication are putting someone s route away from the street at risk.
- You are confident working with complexity. You can hold risk, need and accountability together, making balanced decisions while keeping people s safety, dignity and long-term accommodation sustainment at the centre.
- You build relationships that help things move. Whether you are speaking with someone on the street, a hostel, a Navigator, a statutory service or a community safety partner, you communicate clearly, follow through on actions and keep people focused on solutions.
- You bring practical judgement, emotional resilience and a trauma-informed approach to your work, with the ability to stay calm and purposeful when situations are challenging, stuck or urgent.

Our attractive benefits package includes:
- A salary increase after successfully completing six month's probationary period
- A 37.5 hour working week including flexible working hours (core hours are 10am 4pm) in non-accommodation services
- 25 days annual leave, increasing annually to the maximum 30 days (plus paid Bank Holidays),
- A contributory pension scheme: Single Homeless Project will contribute the equivalent of 5% of your annual salary
- Staff Health Cash Plan and discounts scheme
- Comprehensive and integrated training programme designed specifically to develop the skills and knowledge involved in our work

title: Team Coordinator
description:

Contract type: permanent

Interview dates: 1st stage; w/c 16 November 2026) online/Remote; 2nd stage: 23 November 2026 face to face

Wellcome Collection is part of Wellcome Trust, a global charitable foundation that supports science to build a healthier future for everyone.

Wellcome Collection is a free museum and library exploring health and human experience, where you can enjoy exhibitions, museum and library collections, public events, and a vibrant shop and café. We also publish books and online stories.

This is a great time to join Wellcome Collection as we embark on an exciting period of development. We are looking for two Team Coordinators to join our business operations team. These roles will play an important part in supporting and enabling our teams to deliver on our vision of a world where everyone's experience of health matters.

Where in Wellcome will I be working?

You will be one of three Team Coordinators working within the Strategy, Delivery & Transformation team, reporting to the Wellcome Collections Operations Manager.

Along with the Operations Manager and your fellow Team Coordinators, you will provide high level administrative support across multiple teams and departments within Wellcome Collection

What will I be doing?

Wellcome Collection is a free museum and library that explores connections between health, life and human experience. We are looking for two highly organised and proactive Team Coordinators to provide essential administrative and operational support to our Directorate and Leadership Team. The roles are central to ensuring the smooth running of day-to-day activities, coordinating key meetings and governance processes, managing office operations, and supporting collaboration across teams. Working closely with colleagues across Wellcome Collection, you will help create an efficient, inclusive and well-connected working environment that enables teams to deliver their objectives and the Wellcome Collection strategy.

In this role, you will:
- Provide high-quality administrative support to the Directorate and Leadership Team, including expenses, invoice processing, purchasing, and managing operational activities.
- Coordinate internal and external meetings, preparing agendas, papers and presentations, taking accurate minutes, and tracking actions to completion.
- Organise all-staff meetings, governance meetings, workshops, training sessions, away days, and provide logistical support for events as required.
- Manage onboarding activities for new team members and arrange occasional travel and accommodation for leaders attending external meetings and conferences.
- Oversee office operations, including supplies, equipment, technology requirements, workspace arrangements, and maintaining accurate databases and records.
- Collaborate with colleagues across Wellcome Collection, contributing to a positive, inclusive culture while ensuring administrative cover and support across teams when needed.

Is this job for me?

To be successful in this role, you will bring previous PA, Executive Assistant or administrative experience gained within a busy and fast-paced environment. You will have excellent organisational skills, strong attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple priorities while working to deadlines. You will be confident building relationships with stakeholders at all levels, handling confidential information with discretion, and communicating clearly in both written and verbal formats. Advanced Microsoft Office skills, including SharePoint, are essential, and experience of would be advantageous.

The ideal candidate will have experience managing calendars, preparing meeting papers and presentations, drafting correspondence, taking minutes, and coordinating complex administrative activities. You will be proactive, resourceful and comfortable taking initiative, with a collaborative approach and a commitment to delivering excellent support. Most importantly, you will thrive in a role where organisation, teamwork and attention to detail are critical to enabling the success of others.

To apply for this role please submit an updated CV and answer 2 application questions to demonstrate that you meet the minimum requirements for the role.

- Ability to multi-task, prioritise, take initiative and work to deadlines.
- Well-developed time management skills, including ability to prioritise and reprioritise tasks without compromising quality, organising complex itineraries. As well as good verbal and written communication skills.
- Proficiency in the use of Microsoft Office suite of products (eg Word, Outlook, Excel, SharePoint)
- Ability to deal with people at all levels and deal professionally with confidential material and issues.
- A pragmatic, positive attitude with the desire to work within a high performing team

At Wellcome we have a hybrid way of working which is 3 days in our Euston Road offices (Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday) with the remaining 2 days working either remotely or in the office.

Above all, we need someone who is very organised and good at prioritising.

- Excellent organisational and time-management skills
- Experience coordinating multiple tasks, projects or schedules
- The confidence to prioritise your own workload
- Strong attention to detail
- A calm approach when priorities suddenly change
- Excellent communication skills
- Confidence dealing with a wide range of people
- Good problem-solving ability

description:
Graduate Sales Support Executive

Uxbridge Permanent Full-time

Looking for your first serious commercial career opportunity?

Are you a bright, ambitious graduate with some office, administration or customer service experience who is ready for a role where you can really learn, develop and become an important part of a business?

We are recruiting for an established and successful company in Uxbridge that is looking for someone with potential.

You don't need years of experience. What matters more is that you're switched-on, professional, naturally good with people and eager to learn.

.

You'll work closely with experienced team, supporting a portfolio of business customers and gradually develop a strong understanding of the complete commercial process from quotations and pricing through to orders, projects, purchasing, deliveries and customer account support.

For the right person, it's an excellent opportunity to build a long-term career within a commercial environment.

What will you be doing?

You'll become an important point of contact for customers and provide day-to-day support to the sales and account management team.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Building strong relationships with business customers and responding to their enquiries.
- Preparing quotations and pricing information.
- Managing customer orders from initial enquiry through to successful delivery.
- Helping with tenders, pricing exercises and customer proposals.
- Keeping customers informed and making sure they receive an excellent level of service.
- Coordinating with suppliers and internal departments to ensure orders run smoothly.
- Producing customer reports and analysing information using Excel.
- Maintaining accurate customer and CRM information.
- Investigating queries and finding solutions when things don't go according to plan.
- Learning about products, customers and the wider commercial operation.
- Taking on greater responsibility as your knowledge and confidence develop.

Who are we looking for?

We're particularly interested in candidates at the early stages of their career who can demonstrate genuine potential.

You could be a recent graduate with some office, retail, hospitality or customer-facing experience, or perhaps you're already working in your first commercial role and feel ready for something with greater development opportunities.

You'll ideally have:
- A degree or equivalent level of education.
- Some previous office, administration, customer service or commercial experience.
- Excellent communication skills and a confident telephone manner.
- A genuinely customer-focused approach.
- Strong attention to detail.
- Good numerical and analytical ability.
- Confidence using Microsoft Office, particularly Excel.
- The ability to organise your workload and manage several priorities.
- A proactive attitude you'll ask questions, use your initiative and want to understand how things work.
- The maturity and professionalism to communicate with business customers.

Most importantly, we're looking for someone who is bright, personable, curious and keen to progress.

You won't be expected to arrive knowing everything. You'll receive support while you learn the business, but you'll need the enthusiasm and ability to absorb information quickly and gradually take ownership.

Why consider this opportunity?

This could be a particularly good move if you've completed your degree and are now looking for a role that gives you genuine commercial experience rather than simply another administrative job.

You'll gain exposure to customer account management, sales, pricing, purchasing, projects and business operations while working alongside an experienced team.

There is plenty to learn and scope to develop as you prove yourself.

If you're ambitious, commercially curious and looking for an opportunity where your potential will be recognised, we'd really like to hear from you.

title: Human Resources Coordinator
description:
HR Coordinator EMEA Location: UK Hybrid working
Salary: Competitive, dependent on experience
Working hours: Monday Friday, 8:30am 5:30pm (37.5 hours per week)
Working pattern: 3 days in the office, 2 days working from home

The Opportunity An exciting opportunity has arisen for an experienced and motivated HR Coordinator to join the international HR team of a globally recognised, family-owned organisation with an established reputation for excellence.

This is a varied, hands-on HR generalist position supporting approximately 112 employees across EMEA, with some additional responsibility for the International region. Working within a small, collaborative HR team, you will play an important role in delivering effective HR operations, supporting recruitment activity and ensuring a positive employee experience throughout the employee lifecycle.

The role offers an excellent opportunity for someone with a strong administrative foundation and a broad HR background who is keen to develop their knowledge, take ownership of responsibilities and progress their career within an international business. CIPD qualification is desirable, and support for further professional study may be available.

Key Responsibilities
Recruitment & Talent Acquisition
- Coordinate recruitment activity from vacancy approval through to offer and onboarding, with a strong emphasis on direct sourcing and internal recruitment.
- Advise and support Line Managers on recruitment strategies, candidate sourcing and selection processes.
- Advertise vacancies and utilise LinkedIn and other recruitment platforms to identify and engage potential candidates.
- Review CVs, screen applications, qualify candidates and conduct initial conversations to assess suitability and cultural alignment.
- Coordinate interviews, manage candidate communications and maintain accurate recruitment records.
- Prepare offer letters and employment contracts and coordinate pre-employment checks.
- Organise onboarding and induction processes to ensure a smooth experience for new starters.

HR Administration & Employee Relations
- Provide comprehensive HR administration across the employee lifecycle, including onboarding, employee changes, absence management and offboarding.
- Maintain accurate employee records, personnel files and HR systems, ensuring compliance with GDPR requirements.
- Process employee updates and maintain data across relevant HR systems.
- Support performance reviews, salary and bonus reviews, training coordination and employee development activities.
- Administer annual leave, sickness absence and family-related leave processes.
- Assist with employee engagement initiatives and support meetings and one-to-ones with the HR Director where required.
- Produce HR reports, recruitment trackers and headcount information, ensuring data accuracy and timely reporting.
- Identify opportunities to improve processes and support wider HR projects.

Payroll, Pensions & Benefits
- Coordinate and support UK and European payroll processes, liaising with outsourced providers to ensure accurate and timely submissions.
- Assist with payroll changes, employee amendments and associated documentation.
- Administer employee benefits, including pensions, private medical and dental insurance, life assurance and income protection.
- Liaise with external brokers and benefits providers to manage queries and support day-to-day administration.
- Process pension enrolments and monthly administration, acting as a point of contact for employee enquiries.
- Support international benefits administration and ensure employee changes are accurately recorded.
- Assist with company car administration and other employee benefit arrangements.

International HR & Office Support
- Provide HR operational support across EMEA, with some additional LACM responsibilities.
- Maintain international employee data and coordinate updates with relevant internal teams and external providers.
- Assist with international headcount reporting, recruitment tracking and salary planning activities.
- Provide occasional office management and facilities administration support.
- Help organise company events, employee engagement activities and initiatives that contribute to a positive workplace culture.

About You We are looking for a proactive, organised and self-sufficient HR professional who enjoys working across a broad range of responsibilities and is keen to develop their career.

Ideally, you will have:
- A degree-level qualification.
- At least two years' experience in a generalist HR or HR coordination role.
- A CIPD qualification or a willingness to work towards one.
- A good recruitment background, including candidate screening, direct sourcing and stakeholder management.
- Experience supporting payroll and administering pensions and employee benefits.
- Confidence using LinkedIn and other recruitment tools.
- Strong administrative skills, excellent attention to detail and a high level of accuracy.
- Good analytical skills and the ability to work with HR data, reports and systems.
- Strong IT skills, particularly Microsoft Office; experience with SuccessFactors and ADP would be advantageous.
- Excellent communication skills and the confidence to liaise with employees and managers at all levels.
- The ability to manage competing priorities, meet deadlines and work effectively in a fast-paced environment.
- A practical, solutions-focused approach, with the confidence to take initiative and think outside the box.
- The ability to work independently while contributing positively to a small, collaborative team.

Most importantly, you will be someone who takes ownership, enjoys learning and is motivated to develop their skills within a supportive international environment.
What's on Offer?
- The opportunity to join a globally established and highly regarded organisation.
- Exposure to international HR operations across multiple markets.
- A broad generalist role offering variety and opportunities to expand your HR knowledge.
- A collaborative team environment with access to experienced HR professionals.
- Potential support for further professional development and CIPD studies.
- Hybrid working, with three days in the office and two days from home.

Apply Today If you are an enthusiastic HR professional with a broad generalist background, strong recruitment skills and an appetite to learn, develop and make a difference, we would love to hear from you.

Organise and coordinate meetings, including room bookings, diary management, preparation and circulation of meeting agendas and papers.
