You will also answer queries about the service and will be confident and willing to communicate with neurodivergent people by telephone and face to face, as required. You will need to be well organised in managing clinic appointments, booking and review systems, and coordinating and sending out reports. You will be well supported and highly valued by the Autism Service and will receive regular supervision. The successful applicant will also provide some administrative support to the Adult ADHD Service, as directed by the service leads. Please apply using the NHS Jobs online system. Your application should explain why you are applying for the post, how you believe you would contribute to working in this setting and demonstrate how you meet the requirements of the person specification. Please be aware that the closing date may be brought forward in the event of a high number of applications. Were looking for someone who Has strong administrative and organisational skills, with excellent attention to detail. Can manage competing priorities and work calmly and efficiently in a busy service. Communicates clearly, sensitively and confidently by telephone, email and face to face. Understands the importance of confidentiality, accurate record keeping and timely information sharing. Works well independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team. Ideally has previous administrative experience within a neurodevelopmental, mental health or healthcare service. The usual working hours are 9am- 5pm and will be Monday Friday and there is some flexibility on the days the hours are worked. You will be based at Hollyfield Road in Surbiton although you will also need to be able to travel to our other sites as needed. We encourage you to discuss your flexibility needs with us before applying or during the interview process. While we may not be able to meet every request exactly, we promise to fully consider your needs and accommodate them where possible. Please note that flexible working options may vary depending on the role. When completing your application please refer to full Job Description - this can be found under supporting documents.

title: Receptionist / Administrator
description: Receptionist / Administrator Location: Parkview Surgery, 60 West Drayton Road, Uxbridge, UB8 3LA Hours: 16.5 hours per week Reports to: Reception Manager Please complete the attached Job Application Form and submit it alongside your application. Applications without a completed form will not be considered. Interviews: Tuesday 10 November. Were looking for an enthusiastic, hardworking and approachable person with a positive attitude and a passion for helping others to join our busy practice. This varied role combines patient-facing reception duties with administrative work, helping patients access care and keeping the practice running smoothly. You'll be a confident communicator who listens carefully, puts patients first and handles difficult conversations with empathy and professionalism. Organised and adaptable, you'll respond to changing priorities and take pride in completing tasks accurately and efficiently. A willingness to learn our systems, follow procedures and act on feedback is essential. You'll join a welcoming team that values collaboration, open communication and initiative, with opportunities to develop your skills and make a difference to patients every day. Eligible employees can join the NHS Pension Scheme , with employee and employer contributions made in accordance with scheme rules. This varied role combines welcoming patients, handling telephone enquiries, booking appointments and processing prescription requests with daily administrative duties, including updating patient records, processing clinical documents and actioning emails. You will help patients access appropriate care and support the smooth running of the practice, working flexibly across reception and administration while maintaining accuracy, confidentiality and a professional, helpful approach. Main responsibilities Patient reception and communication Welcome patients and respond to enquiries in person and by telephone with kindness, patience and professionalism. Listen carefully, explain practice processes clearly and direct patients to the appropriate person or service. Remain calm during difficult conversations, help resolve concerns and seek support when needed. Take accurate messages and pass information promptly to the relevant team member. Communicate effectively with patients, carers, colleagues and external services. Appointments and prescriptions Book and manage appointments in line with practice procedures. Receive and pass on home visit requests appropriately. Process repeat prescription requests in accordance with practice guidelines. Administration and patient records Register new patients and update changes to personal details accurately. Maintain patient records using EMIS Web. Process clinical documents through Docman and EMIS in line with training and written protocols. File correspondence and support recalls for medical reviews. Monitor and action incoming emails, referring queries appropriately. Complete general administrative tasks, including photocopying and emailing. Organise and prioritise allocated work, completing tasks accurately and within required timescales. Teamwork and practice support Work flexibly across reception and administration, adapting to changing priorities. Support colleagues and provide agreed cover for staff absence and annual leave. Follow opening, closing and building security procedures. Keep work areas tidy, safe and organised. Undertake other reasonable duties appropriate to the role. Professional responsibilities Maintain patient, staff and practice confidentiality at all times. Follow practice policies, written protocols and information governance requirements. Uphold equality, dignity and respect in all interactions. Follow health and safety, infection prevention and safeguarding procedures, reporting concerns promptly. Complete required training and participate in appraisals. Take responsibility for learning practice processes, acting on feedback and maintaining agreed standards. Contribute suggestions and participate in service improvements, practice meetings or audits when required.

title: Administrator
description: We are looking for an organised and proactive Administrator to join our friendly team, providing vital support across inpatient and community services. This is a varied role where you will be the first point of contact for patients, visitors and colleagues, helping to ensure the smooth day-to-day running of clinical and administrative functions. If you have excellent communication skills, enjoy working in a fast-paced environment, and are confident using Microsoft Office and other IT systems, we would love to hear from you. In return, you'll join a supportive team and play an important role in delivering high-quality patient care and services. Previous Applicants need not apply. Responsible for the day to day administration across intermediate with other members of the team. Responsible for supporting colleagues ensuring work is completed within an agreed timeline. Able to populate reports and collate data on agreed templates This role will act as point of contact for patients and visitors, this will entail being calm, professional and empathetic whilst dealing with potentially sensitive and stressfully situations. This role sits within Ealing Community Partners and will act as point of contact for peers and participate in peer support work. The function of this role is IT based in line with the service objective of being paper light, this will entail fully utilising system one, Microsoft office (including excel and outlook) and other IT equipment such as telephonetics and projectors. The Candidate Pack provides an overview of the key tasks and responsibilities of the role, and the person specification outlines the qualifications, skills, experience and knowledge required. Please view as attached The person specification below is not the full person specification, but outlines the criteria against which your application form will be assessed.

title: Receptionist
description: Join our friendly team at Cranbrook Surgery and make a real difference to our patients and local community. We are looking for a welcoming, organised and motivated Receptionist/Administrator with previous GP surgery experience, who enjoys helping people and working as part of a supportive team. You will be the first point of contact for patients, assisting with appointments, telephone enquiries and essential administrative tasks, while also supporting the Practice Manager with the day-to-day running of the surgery. This is a rewarding opportunity to use your existing skills, develop your experience and contribute to delivering a high-quality service to our patients. You will welcome patients, manage appointment bookings and telephone enquiries, maintain accurate patient records, process incoming correspondence and support the clinical team with daily administrative tasks. You will also assist the Practice Manager with general administration, staff communication, record keeping, updating policies and procedures, monitoring training records and supporting practice operations. You will help ensure patient information is handled confidentially and that the practice runs smoothly, providing a friendly, professional and helpful service to patients and colleagues. Cranbrook Surgery is seeking a friendly, organised and reliable Receptionist/Administrator with previous GP surgery experience to join our busy team in Ilford. Main Duties: Welcome patients and manage appointments and telephone enquiries. Maintain accurate patient records and process correspondence. Provide general administrative support to GPs and clinical staff. Support the Practice Manager with daily operations, staff records, training records and administrative tasks. Maintain confidentiality and follow NHS policies and procedures. Provide a professional, helpful and compassionate service to patients. Essential Requirements: Previous experience working in a GP surgery. Good communication, organisation and IT skills. Knowledge of GP clinical systems, preferably EMIS Web. Ability to work independently and as part of a team. A professional, flexible and confidential approach. We offer a friendly team environment and the opportunity to contribute to high-quality patient care in our local community.

title: Receptionist
description: We are seeking a friendly, organised, reliable and compassionate Receptionist to join our busy NHS GP practice in Southall, serving approximately 5,000 registered patients with a clinical team of 7 GPs. The successful candidate will be the first point of contact for patients, providing a professional, welcoming and efficient reception service. The role involves face-to-face, telephone and online patient enquiries, appointment administration and general administrative duties to support the smooth day-to-day running of the practice. The ideal candidate will have excellent communication and customer service skills, a calm and professional manner, and the ability to work effectively in a busy environment while maintaining patient confidentiality and delivering a high standard of care. 1. Patient Reception and Customer Service Welcome patients and visitors in a friendly, professional and courteous manner. Check patients in for appointments and update their arrival status on the clinical system. Respond to patient enquiries in person, by telephone and through online communication channels. Assist patients with appointment bookings, cancellations and rearrangements in line with practice procedures. Treat all patients with dignity, respect, sensitivity and confidentiality. Communicate effectively with patients from diverse cultural and linguistic backgrounds. Manage difficult or distressed patients calmly and professionally, escalating concerns when necessary. Ensure patients who require additional assistance are supported appropriately. 2. Telephone and Appointment Management Answer incoming telephone calls promptly and professionally. Handle appointment requests in accordance with practice policies and access procedures. Direct calls to the appropriate member of the clinical or administrative team. Take accurate messages and ensure they are passed to the relevant person in a timely manner. Explain practice procedures, appointment arrangements and available services clearly. Recognise when a call may require urgent clinical attention and follow the practice's approved escalation procedures. Never provide clinical advice beyond the receptionist's level of training and authorised responsibilities. Use the practice's clinical computer system, SystmOne, Use the practice's clinical computer system, such as EMIS Web or SystmOne, as applicable. Register patient arrivals and update demographic and contact details in accordance with practice procedures. Maintain accurate electronic records and administrative information. Process incoming and outgoing correspondence as directed. Scan, code or file documents in accordance with practice protocols and staff training. Support the processing of prescription requests, medical records requests and other administrative tasks within the scope of the role. Assist with recalls, patient registrations, appointment lists and other routine administrative work. Ensure all information is recorded accurately and handled securely. Maintain strict patient confidentiality at all times. Comply with UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018, NHS information governance requirements and practice policies. Follow procedures relating to safeguarding children and adults at risk, escalating concerns promptly to the appropriate person. Maintain awareness of confidentiality when speaking on the telephone or at the reception desk. Verify patient identity and follow the practice's procedures before disclosing information. Report any data breaches, confidentiality concerns or incidents to the Practice Manager promptly. Work collaboratively with GPs, nurses, healthcare assistants, managers and other administrative colleagues. Support the daily running of reception, ensuring the reception area remains organised and professional. Assist with incoming post, emails, document handling and general office duties. Follow practice policies, standard operating procedures and health and safety requirements. Attend staff meetings, training sessions and appraisals as required. Assist colleagues during periods of high demand and provide appropriate cover when required. Undertake other reasonable duties consistent with the role and level of responsibility.

title: Receptionist
description: Earl's Court Medical Centre has an exciting opportunity for a Medical Receptionist to join our welcoming and forward thinking Practice team on a part-time basis. Your normal pattern of working will be Monday - Friday, within the hours of 8am-6:30pm (5 hours per day). Interested applicants must have primary care and SystmOne experience. Key Responsibilities include: Greeting and assisting patients at the reception desk Managing appointments, cancellations and patients enquiries Answering telephone calls and directing queries appropriately Processing repeat prescription requests Supporting the administrative and clinical team with day-to-day tasks Maintaining confidentially and ensuring accurate record- keeping Processing ingoing and outgoing patient records This is a patient facing role that requires excellent communication skills, attention to detail, and a calm, efficient approach to working in a fast-paced environment. Reception duties: Ensure an effective and efficient reception service is provided to patients and any other visitors to the Practice. Deal with all general enquiries, explain procedures and make new and follow-up appointments. Using your own judgment and communication skills ensure that patients with no prior appointment but who need urgent consultation are seen in a logical and non-disruptive manner. Explain Practice arrangements and formal requirements to new patients and those seeking temporary cover and ensure procedures are completed. Receive and make telephone calls as required. Divert calls and take messages, ensuring accuracy of detail and prompt appropriate delivery. Enter requests for home visits into the home visits book, ensuring careful recording of all relevant details and where necessary refer to Duty Doctor. Action repeat prescription requests and ensure that they are ready for collection by the patient within 72 hours, in line with Practice protocol. Take action on clinicians requests for further information/patient contact information etc. (including computerised practice notes), ensuring completion of all associated paperwork. Advise patients of relevant charges for private (non-General Medical Services) services, accept payment and issue receipts for same. Enter patient information on to the computer as required. Prepare clinical rooms for surgeries, supply prescription forms and record numbers in use and ensure adequate supplies of consumables (including bottles, couch rolls, test request forms etc.). Premises: Open up premises at the start of the day when first to arrive, de-activate alarm and make all necessary preparations to receive patients. When last to leave at the end of the day, ensure that the building is totally secured, internal lights are off and the alarm activated. Ensure that all new patients are registered onto the computer system promptly and accurately Make and serve refreshments for meetings, ensure the kitchen is kept clean and tidy and air and tidy the waiting room in turn with other staff. Covering colleagues holiday and sick cover as required. Process incoming and outgoing mail according to practice protocols. Record actions taken in patient record where appropriate or in accordance with practice protocols. Complete other Daily/ Weekly and Monthly core tasks to support to smooth running of the reception area Any other administration duties as necessitated by the needs of the practice. Confidentiality : In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately. In the performance of the duties outlined in this Job Description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, Practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the Practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential. Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the Practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the Practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data. Health & Safety: The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the Practice Health & Safety Policy, to include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to Practice guidelines Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards Reporting potential risks identified Act as Chaperone when requested by clinician and in accordance with the Chaperone policy. Equality and Diversity: The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognises the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with the Practice policies and procedures, and current legislation Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues Behaving in a manner which is welcoming to the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Personal/Professional Development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the Practice as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of their own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for their own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work Quality : The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the Practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload and resources Communication : The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognise peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly Contribution to the Implementation of Services: The post-holder will: Apply Practice policies, standards and guidance Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work Participate in audit where appropriate

title: Receptionist
description: We are looking for 2 Recepetionists to join our team. Working 16.5 hours per week, shifts will vary from mornings and afternoons. MUST HAVE GP & EMIS EXPERIENCE. The Receptionist will support staff with the distribution of information, messages and enquiries for the clinical team, liaising with multidisciplinary team members and external agencies such as secondary care and community service providers. The post-holder will be an integral part of the general practice team. Welcome patients and visitors in a professional, friendly, and courteous manner. Answer telephone calls promptly, deal with enquiries, take messages, and direct calls to the appropriate staff. Book, amend, and cancel appointments in accordance with practice procedures. Register new patients and update patient records, ensuring information is accurate and up to date. Manage patient enquiries face-to-face, by telephone, and via online communication systems. Handle confidential patient information in accordance with GDPR, confidentiality requirements, and practice policies. To provide a professional, friendly, and efficient reception service to patients, visitors, and healthcare professionals, ensuring the smooth day-to-day running of the GP practice. The postholder will support the clinical and administrative teams while maintaining patient confidentiality and delivering a high standard of customer service.

title: Receptionist

The practice is situated in a pleasant part of Blackheath in South East London with good transport links and local shops. The position is for 22 hours per week over four days, based on a seven week rolling rota. Please note that the rota is variable and you will be working different days over a seven week period. This is based on a 7am start and 12.30pm finish 8am start and 1pm finish, 1pm start and 6pm finish, 1.30pm start with a 7pm finish. This can vary , depending on the needs of the practice during sickness and annual leave. Flexibility is essential. Saturday mornings are part of our enhanced access service and there is the option to work these sessions on a rotation basis. We are a friendly team, who are supportive of each other and there will be opportunity to develop new skills. Duties include: Covering reception desk, answering telephone calls, booking appointments via AccuRx triage system, dealing with patient queries, order prescriptions, process admin duties for clinical staff, general administration such as filing and liaising with other health care providers in a professional manner, and processing clinical letters through the Docman system. The duties are variable, depending on what is required on the day. Candidates must have strong communication skills, be friendly, reliable and willing to learn. The applicant must have the ability to prioritise workload. Applicants must have the ability to work within a team, have experience of EMIS, AccuRx and Docman and IT skills. Previous experience of working in General Practice is essential, further training will be available for any candidates that show a passion for learning. Job Description Main duties include: Covering reception desk greeting patients and visitors with a professional and friendly manner. Manage the booking system efficiently, signposting patients to the relevant services. Answering incoming calls, respond to queries and manage email correspondence promptly. Assist clinicians as needed, including handling paperwork, stocking consultation rooms and daily end of day duties to ensure the rooms are meeting infection control standards. Manage office supplies, handling incoming/outgoing post and perform general administrative duties. Maintain accurate patient records and ensure confidentiality. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data. The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice Health & Safety Policy. The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues. The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment. The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognise needs of people for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly.

title: Service Administrator
description: To provide administrative support for the Mental Health Practitioner Service, Health & Wellbeing Coach Service and the Social Prescribing Service. To ensure that all patients referred in are logged and triaged to the appropriate member of each service. To contact patients and provide a service introduction to ensure that expectations are clear. To book initial consultations on behalf of service staff and send reminders to patients. Other agreed administrative tasks as requested and agreed with the service leads, such as meeting notes. To support the Service Leads and H&WB Manager with service reporting, to provide visibility to the GP practices around work done. Responsibilities 1. Referral triage for each service. 2. Booking in and carrying out introduction calls for referrals and sending back inappropriate referrals to referrers. 3. Booking in the initial consultation for each patient with the appropriate service team member. 4. Day to day management and oversight of appointment books, active patient load as well as waiting lists. 5. Sending appointment reminder texts. 6. Oversight of DNAs and focused work on improving the current rates for each service. 7. Manage and oversight of complaints & learning events to ensure a reduction of issues especially around patient bookings. 8. Last minute staff sickness appointment cancellations and communication. 9. Ongoing admin support in the office for team members who travel between many different sites/practices such as letter printing and posting letters to patients. 10. If capacity allows a. Supporting service audit completion b. Uploading compliments to teamnet c. Managing the H&WB Teamnet page d. Supporting at all-staff meetings. e. Helping to organize/attend community events/sessions. 11. Any other reasonable duties required by the Service Leads or Health & Wellbeing Manager in support of the services. This team member would be based in head office at Thomas Wall. Team working Work with the Health & Wellbeing Service Leads and team members. Work with the practice & Sutton PCNs teams to ensure delivery of services and programmes. Actively engage in the performance cycle to identify training and support requirements. Communication The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members as required Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognise peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly

title: Receptionist/Administrator

Book, cancel and rearrange appointments according to practice procedures. Register new patients and update patient information accurately. Receiving patients, consulting with members of practice team, processing personal and telephone requests for appointments, telephone consultations and ensuring callers are directed to the appropriate healthcare professional. description: This position is five day a week (Mon to Fri) on site with no remote working. The trust does not offer visa sponsorship for this post. Tyson West 1 is part of Bethlem Royal Hospital. We offer services for men, aged 18-65, who have acute mental illness and require 24 hour hospital care. Acute illnesses start quickly and have distressing symptoms.We provide care for people who live in the London Borough of Croydon.We offer psychiatric assessment, care and treatment in hospital, which helps to reduce the risk to self and others.Our service brings together teams of health and social care professionals, including nurses, psychologists, OTs, social workers and psychiatrists. This position is five day a week on site with no remote working. We are looking for a highly organised, efficient, flexible and proactive person with excellent communication skills to work in the busy post, and who can balance work demands along with the changing needs of the service. The role requires the post holder to communicate with patients, ward staff and visitors, and to develop collaborative working relationships with colleagues and external agencies. The post holder must have an excellent telephone manner, good IT skills with experience using Microsoft Office packages (Work, Excel and Outlook) . Other tasks include, but not limited to, ordering of stationery, processing of post, scanning, monitoring and ordering ward stock and other tasks (see job description). You must be able to prioritise your workload, be effective at implementing good working practices as well as having a flexible and proactive approach to work in order to cover colleagues when required. Be responsible for the provision of a high-quality reception and administrative service for a busy acute ward. Reception:To provide an effective and efficient reception and administrative services, which will include dealing with telephone enquiries, taking accurate messages and pass them promptly to the appropriate member of the team. Dealing with the public, face-to-face, in a courteous andkind manner and identifying and informing as appropriate the responsible professional worker. To monitor supplies of patient information such as welcome packs.Administration:To assist in providing a comprehensive administrative service to the multi-disciplinary teams, which include but not limited to data inputting patient information, scanning documents and uploading to patient database. Maintaining efficient and effective administration systems to support the needs of the service, working with other members of the admin team as appropriate to achieve this. To assist in providing accurate and efficient data entry into Trust information systems and to assist in the collection of statistical information for the Trust. To assist in the booking of interpreters, taxis etc. Service Requirements:To undertake any other duties as required for the service by the Business Manager or Team Leaders.To deliver a high standard of customer care, representative or the service and the overall Trust objectives and commitments. Exercise diplomacy and professionalism, confidentially and equality standards in accordance with all Trust policies. Staff DevelopmentTo attend regular supervision and annual appraisal meetings. To participate in any training and developmental needs as required by the Business Manager.To complete all identified mandatory training and ensure this is kept up-to-date.

title: Care Navigator/Receptionist & Administrator
description: As the first point of contact for patients, you will play a key role in delivering excellent customer service and supporting the smooth running of the practice. Duties include welcoming patients, handling telephone and face-to-face enquiries, responding to emails, processing prescription requests, filing and coding clinical correspondence and referrals, supporting safeguarding processes, undertaking site checks, monitoring stock levels, and helping maintain a safe environment. Working as part of a team of four, you will contribute to a shared workload and help ensure patients receive the right support at the right time. The role is offered on a split rota of 07:45-13:45 (Week 1) and 13:00-19:00 (Week 2) . Previous experience in a GP practice or similar patient-facing role is essential. Applicants must have 6-12 months' experience and be proficient in EMIS Web . The successful candidate must deliver excellent patient care and customer service while maintaining professionalism and accuracy. If you are a reliable team player with excellent communication skills, attention to detail and a commitment to patient care, we would love to hear from you. As a Patient Care Navigator / Receptionist / Administrator, you will be the first point of contact for patients and visitors, providing a professional, friendly and efficient service. You will welcome patients, respond to enquiries in person and by telephone, and support patients in accessing the most appropriate services. The role includes processing prescription requests, responding to emails, filing and coding clinical correspondence, maintaining accurate patient records, processing referrals via NHS e-Referral Service, actioning eConsults as directed by the clinical team, managing appointments, registering new patients, and handling general enquiries. You will be expected to cover colleagues' absences where required, attend practice meetings, maintain a tidy reception area, support patient recall programmes, and undertake additional administrative tasks as directed by the Practice Manager. You will support safeguarding processes, undertake site checks, monitor stock levels, report issues appropriately, and help ensure the premises are safe and secure. Working as part of a team of four, you will share workloads, support colleagues during busy periods, and contribute to a positive, patient-focused environment. Excellent communication skills, attention to detail, flexibility and a commitment to high-quality patient care are essential. Job description Key Responsibilities Patient Care & Reception Meet and greet patients and visitors in a professional and welcoming manner. Assist patients with enquiries, signposting them to the most appropriate service where necessary. Respond to patient queries both in person and over the telephone. Support patients with appointments, registrations and general practice services. Always maintain patient confidentiality. Administrative Duties Process incoming hospital correspondence, including filing and clinical coding of letters and reports. Process prescription requests accurately and efficiently. Respond promptly to emails received by the practice. Maintain accurate patient records and update information as required. Undertake general administrative tasks to support the smooth running of the practice. Safeguarding & Compliance Identify and escalate any safeguarding concerns or requests appropriately. Follow all practice policies, procedures and information governance requirements. Support the practice in maintaining a safe environment for patients, staff and visitors. Premises & Operational Support Carry out routine site and building checks as required. Ensure the building is secure at opening and closing times. Monitor and maintain appropriate stock levels of clinical and office supplies. Report maintenance issues or concerns promptly. Teamworking Work collaboratively as part of a team of four within the reception and administration function. Support colleagues during busy periods and contribute positively to team objectives. Participate fully in the shared workload and demonstrate flexibility where required. Promote a positive, patient-focused culture throughout the practice.

title: ED Receptionist
company: Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust
advertiser_name: Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust
description: To provide an efficient and effective front of house administration and clerical support service for the emergency department always projecting a positive and professional image. Receptionists working within the Emergency Department are the first point of contact for patients and visitors attending the department and are expected to demonstrate a high level of professionalism, care, courtesy and respect when greeting patients. The role of the ED Receptionist is based in the front reception setting in the heart of a busy ED Department. The role involves providing front of house for the department. Proven medical administrative background, a good telephone manner and excellent customer care skills and advanced computer skills are essential. You need to be highly motivated with excellent interpersonal skills. The role can be demanding but it is also extremely interesting and varied with no two days being the same. You will need to be confident in working with the public in a fast paced ever changing environment. You must also be able to work under pressure under your own initiative whilst being part of a supportive team. Working in a busy environment, Emergency Department Receptionists will register patients into the department, answer telephone queries and undertake a range of administrative duties to support the effective running of the department. Please see attached job description & person specification for more detailed information about this role and working at Royal Free London NHS Foundation Trust.

title: GP Receptionist
description: Join Dr Sharma & Rai Practice Group as a full-time GP Receptionist, primarily based at Heathway Medical Centre in Dagenham. You will be a welcoming first point of contact for patients and a valued member of our friendly and supportive practice team. We are looking for someone reliable, organised and confident communicating with people face to face. Previous GP reception experience is an advantage, but not essential. We also welcome applicants with strong customer service experience who enjoy helping people, can manage a variety of tasks and are quick to learn new online systems. Good IT skills, excellent communication and a friendly, professional approach are essential. This is a fixed-term position until 8 August 2027, with the possibility of extension. The role is 37.5 hours per week, working varied shifts between 07:45 and 18:30, Monday to Friday, excluding bank holidays. Pay is £12.71 per hour. Our wider practice group offers opportunities to gain experience, develop new skills and apply for permanent positions as vacancies arise. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early if sufficient applications are received. Early applications are encouraged. As a GP Receptionist, you will play an important role in supporting patients and helping the practice run smoothly. Your daily responsibilities will include: Welcoming patients and visitors, providing friendly and professional assistance. Responding to patient enquiries face to face, by telephone and through online systems. Helping patients access appropriate services, including assisting with online appointment requests. Using our clinical system (EMIS Web) and other digital platforms to manage patient information and administrative tasks. Processing patient requests, including prescriptions, test-related enquiries and general correspondence. Supporting GPs, nurses and other team members with day-to-day administrative duties. Maintaining accurate records and handling confidential information appropriately. Working closely with colleagues to provide a positive experience for patients. Full training and guidance on our practice systems and procedures will be provided. We value teamwork, initiative and a willingness to learn. Job Description GP Receptionist Organisation: Dr Sharma & Rai Practice Group Primary Location: Heathway Medical Centre, Dagenham Contract: Full-time, fixed-term until 8 August 2027, with the possibility of extension Hours: 37.5 hours per week, with varied shifts between 07:45 and 18:30, Monday to Friday, excluding bank holidays. To provide a friendly, professional and efficient reception and administrative service to patients, visitors and healthcare professionals. The GP Receptionist plays an important role in supporting patients to access healthcare services, maintaining accurate records and assisting the wider practice team with daily operations. The successful candidate will be based primarily at Heathway Medical Centre, with occasional cover at other practices within Dr Sharma & Rai Practice Group where required. 1. Patient Reception and Customer Service Welcome patients and visitors in a friendly, helpful and professional manner. Act as a first point of contact for patients attending the practice. Respond to patient enquiries face to face, by telephone and through digital communication systems. Assist patients with appointment requests and provide information about available services. Support patients who may require additional assistance accessing healthcare services. Communicate clearly and sensitively with patients from different backgrounds and with varying needs. Handle patient concerns and difficult situations calmly, professionally and respectfully, referring matters to senior colleagues when appropriate. Maintain a welcoming, organised and professional reception environment. 2. Appointment Management and Patient Access Support patients with accessing appointments and services in accordance with practice procedures. Assist patients in using online consultation and appointment request systems. Provide guidance on accessing the NHS App and other available digital services. Process appointment requests, cancellations and changes as directed by practice procedures. Signpost patients to appropriate services using established practice guidance and care navigation procedures. Escalate urgent concerns or clinical queries to the appropriate healthcare professional without providing clinical advice. Help ensure patients receive clear and accurate information about practice services. 3. Clinical Systems and Digital Administration Use EMIS Web and other practice systems to access and update patient information accurately. Process patient requests received through online platforms and electronic communication systems. Scan, upload and attach relevant documents to patient records. Record patient interactions and administrative activities appropriately. Support the processing of incoming correspondence and electronic documents. Maintain accurate records while following confidentiality and information governance requirements. Learn and confidently use new digital systems as introduced by the practice. 4. General Administrative Duties Process routine patient enquiries relating to prescriptions, test requests, referrals and other practice services in accordance with established procedures. Assist with the collection and distribution of forms, letters and other documents. Support the preparation and processing of administrative correspondence. Liaise with hospitals, pharmacies, community healthcare providers and other external organisations when required. Maintain accurate records and ensure administrative tasks are completed in a timely manner. Support clinical and non-clinical colleagues with general administrative tasks. Assist with maintaining an organised and efficient reception and office environment. 5. Teamwork and Communication Work collaboratively with reception colleagues, GPs, nurses, healthcare assistants and administrative staff. Communicate effectively with colleagues to support the smooth running of the practice. Provide reception cover and assistance to colleagues when required. Share relevant information with appropriate team members to ensure continuity of service. Participate in team meetings, training and development activities. Contribute positively to a respectful, supportive and professional working environment. 6. Confidentiality, Safety and Professional Standards Maintain strict patient confidentiality and comply with data protection and information governance requirements. Follow practice policies and procedures, including safeguarding, health and safety, infection prevention and control, and equality and diversity. Recognise and appropriately escalate safeguarding concerns or situations requiring clinical attention. Treat all patients, visitors and colleagues with dignity, respect and sensitivity. Work within the boundaries of the receptionist role and seek guidance when necessary. Maintain professional standards of conduct and appearance. Full induction and training on practice-specific systems and procedures will be provided. Previous experience in a GP practice and familiarity with EMIS Web would be advantageous but are not essential. We welcome candidates with experience in customer-facing roles who demonstrate strong communication skills, a positive attitude, good computer skills and a willingness to learn. As part of Dr Sharma & Rai Practice Group, employees may have opportunities to develop additional skills, gain experience across different practice functions and apply for permanent vacancies as they arise. The successful candidate must be flexible in their working hours and available for different shifts within the practice's core opening hours. This job description outlines the main responsibilities of the position and may be reviewed or adapted to meet the operational needs of the practice, within the appropriate scope of the role.

title: GP Receptionist
description: Join our friendly team at St Katharine Docks Practice , a welcoming single-handed GP surgery set in the beautiful surroundings of St Katharine Docks, just moments from the Tower of London. We pride ourselves on providing high-quality, personalised care to our patients and creating a supportive, professional, and inclusive workplace. We are looking for a Receptionist to provide cover , helping to ensure the smooth running of our busy front desk. As the first point of contact for patients, youll play a vital role in making every patient feel welcome, listened to, and supported. Youll handle calls, manage appointments, process correspondence, and assist the GP and wider team in delivering excellent service. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys helping others, communicates clearly and kindly, and can stay calm under pressure. Youll need to be organised, confident using computers, and committed to maintaining confidentiality at all times. In return, we offer a friendly working environment, on-the-job training, and opportunities for personal development. Youll be part of a small, close-knit team where your contribution truly makes a difference to the lives of our patients and the success of our practice. If youre reliable, compassionate, and looking for a rewarding role in the heart of London, wed love to hear from you. Welcome and assist patients and visitors in person and over the telephone in a professional and friendly manner. Manage incoming calls, respond to general enquiries, and direct calls as appropriate. Schedule and manage patient appointments using the practice clinical system - EMIS Web. Register new patients and update existing patient information accurately. Handle incoming and outgoing post and emails. Obtain external medical reports, test results, and other documentation as required. Scan and file correspondence and clinical documents. Maintain a tidy, organised, and welcoming reception area. Safeguard patient confidentiality and comply with GDPR and NHS data protection requirements. Provide reassurance and support to patients, maintaining a calm and caring approach. Carry out general administrative duties as required by the GP or Practice Manager. Ensure an effective and efficient reception service is provided to patients and any other visitors to the Practice. Deal with all general enquiries, explain procedures and make new and follow-up appointments. Using your own judgment and communication skills ensure that patients with no prior appointment but who need urgent consultation are seen in a logical and non-disruptive manner. Explain Practice arrangements and formal requirements to new patients and those seeking temporary cover and ensure procedures are completed. Receive and make telephone calls as required. Divert calls and take messages, ensuring accuracy of detail and prompt appropriate delivery. Enter requests for home visits into the home visits book, ensuring careful recording of all relevant details and where necessary refer to Duty Doctor. Action repeat prescription requests and ensure that they are ready for collection by the patient within 48 hours, in line with Practice protocol. Take action on clinicians requests for further information/patient contact information etc. including computerised practice notes, ensuring completion of all associated paperwork. Advise patients of relevant charges for private (non-General Medical Services) services, accept payment and issue receipts for same. Enter patient information on to the computer as required. Prepare clinical rooms for surgeries, supply prescription forms and record numbers in use and ensure adequate supplies of consumables - including bottles, couch rolls, test request forms etc..

title: GP Receptionist / Administrator
description: Part-Time GP Receptionist/Administrator We are looking for an experienced, part-time GP Receptionist/Administrator to join our friendly and busy team. The successful candidate will be organised, calm under pressure, confident on the telephone, and able to work independently as well as part of a team. Previous experience in a GP practice is preferred, along with good administrative skills and a commitment to providing a helpful, professional and compassionate service to our patients. This is a permanent, part-time position with the following working hours: Monday to Thursday: 12:30 pm 6:30 pm Friday: 8:30 am 6:30 pm Flexibility to cover colleagues annual leave is also required. We are looking for someone reliable and enthusiastic who would like to become a valued, long-term member of our team. Providing front-desk reception and dealing with patient queries. Answering telephone calls and booking appointments. Supporting the GP on duty with triage administration. Actioning online requests and following up queries. Managing clinical documents. Carrying out general administrative duties. Working independently and as part of a team. Maintaining patient confidentiality at all times. Prioritising workload and remaining calm in a busy environment. Key Responsibilities and Requirements The role involves providing front-desk reception services, answering telephone calls, responding to patient queries, booking appointments and supporting the GP on duty with triage administration. The successful candidate will be organised, reliable and able to work independently as well as part of a team. They will be confident in prioritising their workload, managing competing demands and remaining calm and professional in a busy environment, while maintaining strict patient confidentiality at all times. Previous experience in a GP practice is preferred, particularly familiarity with EMIS Web, Accurx, Docman and the ERS referral system . Good communication, administrative and organisational skills, together with a friendly and professional approach to patient care, are essential.

title: Medical Receptionist
description: The Law Medical Group Practice is seeking a reliable and organised Receptionist to join the team at its Wembley branch. The practice is committed to delivering high quality primary care services to its local community and ensuring smooth day to day patient flow through efficient administrative and reception support. The successful candidate will play a key role in supporting the clinical and non clinical teams by undertaking a range of front of house and administrative duties. This will include managing appointments through EMIS, handling patient queries, processing incoming correspondence and ensuring information is accurately directed to the relevant clinicians in a timely manner. The role will involve full front of house responsibilities, including welcoming and directing patients, responding to queries and providing a professional and efficient service both in person and over the telephone. Working Pattern: Part Time, 27.5 Hours per Week The working hours are Monday to Friday, 1:00 pm to 6:30 pm. Please note: The working days and hours are non negotiable . Applicants must be able to commit to this working pattern. Eligibility: Applicants must be UK citizens and have a minimum of five years of work experience in the UK. The role involves providing comprehensive reception support to the multidisciplinary team within the practice. Key responsibilities include managing patient interactions, handling incoming correspondence, and ensuring accurate distribution of information to clinicians. The position includes front-desk duties such as greeting and directing patients, managing the appointment system using EMIS , booking appointments, responding to patient enquiries, and supporting the smooth and efficient day-to-day operation of the practice. The following are the core responsibilities of the Administrator/Receptionist . There may occasionally be a requirement to carry out other duties depending on workload, operational needs, and staffing levels. Primary Responsibilities Receive and process correspondence from hospitals, external healthcare providers, and other agencies. Scan and upload documents onto the EMIS clinical system, ensuring accurate patient record management. Review and appropriately allocate documents within EMIS , forwarding them to the relevant clinician for review and action. Initiate and respond to requests from patients, practice staff, and external healthcare agencies in a professional and timely manner. Photocopy and prepare documentation as required by clinicians and practice staff. Provide cover for colleagues during periods of absence to ensure continuity of service. Accurately input patient information and updates into EMIS where required. Manage and resolve patient queries efficiently, escalating issues where appropriate. Maintain a clean, organised, and efficient reception environment at all times. Support the clinical team with day-to-day operational tasks as required. Complete tasks relating to patient results, correspondence, and clinical letters where appropriate. Demonstrate flexibility and adaptability in managing changing workloads and priorities to ensure the smooth operation of the practice. Use EMIS and other digital systems effectively for patient record management, appointment scheduling, and internal communication. Secondary Responsibilities In addition to the primary responsibilities, the Medical Receptionist may also be required to: Maintain and monitor the practice appointment system using EMIS . Process appointment requests received in person, by telephone, and via online systems. Answer incoming telephone calls and direct them appropriately or deal with enquiries where possible. Signpost patients to the appropriate healthcare professional or NHS service. Support practice audits and administrative reviews as directed by management. Process incoming electronic communications and documents where required. Scan and attach patient-related documentation accurately to patient records within EMIS . Carry out opening and closing procedures in accordance with the practice rota and operational requirements.
